chapter.li: LEChapter14 Verse1 And it came to pass in Iconium that they both went together into the synagogue of the Jews and so spoke that a great multitude both of the Jews and also of the Greeks believed. VerseEnd Verse2 But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and made their minds poisoned against the brethren. VerseEnd Verse3 For a long time therefore stayed they, speaking boldly in the Lord, which gave testimony unto the word of his grace, and granted signs and wonders to be done by their hands. VerseEnd Verse4 But the multitude of the city was divided, and part held with the Jews and part with the apostles. VerseEnd Verse5 And when there was an assault made, both of the Gentiles and also of the Jews with their rulers, to treat them spitefully and to stone them, VerseEnd Verse6 they were aware of it and fled unto Lystra and Derbe, cities of Lycaonia, and unto the region that lies round about. VerseEnd Verse7 And there they preached the gospel. VerseEnd

Verse8 And there sat a certain man at Lystra, impotent in his feet, being a cripple from his mother’s womb who never had walked. VerseEnd Verse9 The same heard Paul speak, who, steadfastly beholding him and perceiving that he had faith to be healed, VerseEnd Verse10 said with a loud voice, Stand upright on your feet. And he leaped and walked. VerseEnd Verse11 And when the people saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices, saying in the speech of Lycaonia, The gods have come down to us in the likeness of men. VerseEnd Verse12 And they called Barnabas, Jupiter, and Paul, Mercury, because he was the chief speaker. VerseEnd Verse13 Then the priest of Jupiter, who was before their city, brought oxen and garlands unto the gates, and would have done sacrifice with the people, VerseEnd Verse14 which when the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard this, they rent their clothes and ran in among the people, crying out VerseEnd Verse15 and saying, Sirs, why do you do these things! We also are men of like passions with you, and preach unto you that you should turn from these vanities unto the living God, who made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and all things that are therein; VerseEnd Verse16 who in times past suffered all nations to walk in their own ways. VerseEnd Verse17 Nevertheless, he left not himself without witness, in that he did good, and gave us rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness. VerseEnd Verse18 And with these sayings, they scarcely restrained the people, that they did not do sacrifice unto them. VerseEnd

Verse19 And there came there certain Jews from Antioch and Iconium, who persuaded the people, and, having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing he had been dead. VerseEnd Verse20 Nevertheless, as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up and came into the city; and the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe. VerseEnd

Verse21 And when they had preached the gospel to that city and had taught many, they returned again to Lystra, and to Iconium, and Antioch, VerseEnd Verse22 confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God. VerseEnd Verse23 And when they had ordained them elders in every church and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord, on whom they believed. VerseEnd

Verse24 And after they had passed throughout Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia. VerseEnd Verse25 And when they had preached the word in Perga, they went down into Attalia, VerseEnd Verse26 and from there sailed to Antioch — from where they had been recommended to the grace of God for the work which they fulfilled. VerseEnd Verse27 And when they had come and had gathered the church together, they rehearsed all that God had done with them and how he had opened the door of faith unto the Gentiles. VerseEnd Verse28 And there they stayed for a long time with the disciples. VerseEnd

LEChapter15 Verse1 And certain men who came down from Judea taught the brethren and said, Except you be circumcised after the manner of Moses, you cannot be saved. VerseEnd Verse2 When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and disputation with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas and certain other of them should go up to Jerusalem, unto the apostles and elders about this question. VerseEnd Verse3 And being brought on their way by the church, they passed through Phoenicia and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles; and they caused great joy unto all the brethren. VerseEnd Verse4 And when they had come to Jerusalem, they were received of the church and of the apostles and elders, and they declared all things that God had done with them. VerseEnd

Verse5 But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees who believed, saying that it was needful to circumcise them and to command them to keep the law of Moses; VerseEnd Verse6 and the apostles and elders came together to consider of this matter. VerseEnd Verse7 And when there had been much disputing, Peter rose up and said unto them, Men and brethren, you know that a good while ago God made choice among us that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel and believe. VerseEnd Verse8 And God, who knows the hearts, bore them witness, giving them the holy ghost even as he did unto us, VerseEnd Verse9 and put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith. VerseEnd Verse10 Now, therefore, why do you test God, to put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear? VerseEnd Verse11 But we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ we shall be saved, even as they. VerseEnd Verse12 Then all the multitude kept silence and gave audience to Barnabas and Paul declaring what miracles and wonders God had wrought among the Gentiles by them. VerseEnd

Verse13 And after they had held their peace, James answered, saying, Men and brethren, listen unto me. VerseEnd Verse14 Simon has declared how God at the first did visit the Gentiles, to take out of them a people for his name. VerseEnd Verse15 And to this agree the words of the prophets, as it is written: VerseEnd Verse16 After this, I will return and will build again the tabernacle of David which is fallen down, and I will build again the ruins thereof, and I will set it up, VerseEnd Verse17 that the residue of men might seek after the Lord, and all the Gentiles upon whom my name is called, says the Lord, who does all these things. VerseEnd Verse18 Known unto God are all his works from the beginning of the world. VerseEnd Verse19 Wherefore, my sentence is that we trouble not them who, from among the Gentiles, are turned to God, VerseEnd Verse20 but that we write unto them that they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood; VerseEnd Verse21 for Moses of old time has in every city them that preach him, being read in the synagogues every Sabbath day. VerseEnd

Verse22 Then it pleased the apostles and elders, with the whole church, to send chosen men of their own company to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: namely Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas — chief men among the brethren. VerseEnd Verse23 And they wrote letters by them after this manner: The apostles, and elders, and brethren send greeting unto the brethren who are of the Gentiles in Antioch, and Syria, and Cilicia. VerseEnd Verse24 Forasmuch as we have heard that certain men who went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, You must be circumcised and keep the law — to whom we gave no such commandment VerseEnd — Verse25 it seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul, VerseEnd Verse26 men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. VerseEnd Verse27 We have sent therefore Judas and Silas, who shall also tell you the same things by mouth; VerseEnd Verse28 for it seemed good to the holy ghost and to us to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things: VerseEnd Verse29 that you abstain from food offered to idols, and from blood, and from things strangled, and from fornication, from which if you keep yourselves, you shall do well. Farewell. VerseEnd

Verse30 So when they were dismissed, they came to Antioch, and when they had gathered the multitude together, they delivered the epistle, VerseEnd Verse31 which when they had read, they rejoiced for the consolation. VerseEnd Verse32 And Judas and Silas, being prophets also themselves, exhorted the brethren with many words and confirmed them. VerseEnd Verse33 And after they had remained there a space, they were let go in peace from the brethren unto the apostles, VerseEnd Verse34 notwithstanding it pleased Silas to continue there still. VerseEnd Verse35 Paul also and Barnabas continued in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord with many others also. VerseEnd
